title: Quench crust: dust before, slabs after
question: Is this the 'chunks instead of a pile of dust' you asked for? Watch what leaves the crust as it founders - single pixels, or pieces?
context_md:
Your verdict on the last crust card was **"the stone sinking to the bottom is better, but it would be better with chunks instead of pile of dust."**

I measured why before changing anything. The pond quench produced **572 structural failures, and 382 of them were a single cell** (sizes `1:382 2:92 3-5:85 6-7:8 8-15:5`). The engine declines to make a chunk below 6 cells and cannot make a rigid body below 8, so 97.7% of those failures could never reach the fragment ladder at all. Stone's six fragment sizes were already the widest in the game and sat downstream of a gate that had refused 559 times: no amount of tuning them could have worked.

The cause was that quench mints a few scattered cells a frame and each one was judged, alone, the instant it appeared. Fresh stone now gets about a second to knit together with whatever is quenching beside it before the world asks whether it is holding itself up.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| mean cells per failure | 1.7 | **6.0** |
| largest single failure | 12 | **83** |
| failures of 8+ cells | 5 | **137** |
| chunk bodies in flight | 2 | **16** |

Both clips are the same seed, same scene, same 90 frames. Nothing else differs.

**Also worth your eye:** the crust hangs for about a second before it goes. You said a brief hang was fine if it bought chunks -- this is what that costs, and I want to know whether it reads as a crust forming or as a bug.
